title: Computer Vision: Images as Data
status: Draft practice quiz — teacher review required
instructions: Ten questions drawn from the worked examples in the Course and Laboratory. Some questions require selecting all correct answers. Exact matches earn one point.

questions.prompt: What does I[row][column] return for a grayscale image?
options: The number of images in a folder
questions.explanation: An image can be represented as a 2D table of pixel intensities.

questions.prompt: How many channel values are in a 6-by-4 RGB image with three channels per pixel?
What is the simple channel average for RGB=(120,180,240)?
Using 0.2126R+0.7152G+0.0722B, which result is closest for RGB=(120,180,240)?
With T=128, rule input<T→0 else 255, what happens to value 127?
questions.explanation: 127 is below 128, so it becomes black.

questions.prompt: With T=128, how is intensity 128 classified?
questions.explanation: Equality belongs to the ≥ threshold branch, giving 255.

questions.prompt: A 3×3 patch contains four values 255 and five zero. What is its mean, approximately?
Why must a filter define what happens at image boundaries?
options: Some neighbouring coordinates lie outside the image
All image borders must be black
Every 3×3 kernel has nine zero coefficients
questions.explanation: Padding, replication and valid-only convolution produce different results.

questions.prompt: Which observations about filters are correct?
options: Smoothing can reduce isolated pixel noise
questions.explanation: Processing trades noise removal against preservation of detail.

questions.prompt: A filter response equals 1020 but the output image stores 8-bit grayscale values. What must be specified?
questions.explanation: An 8-bit output stores only 0–255; the display rule matters.
